insider_note: secx tanx is the derivative of secx — a standard derivative worth having memorised cold, since it is the trigger for recognising this f+f′ pairing instantly.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Identify f(x) and f′(x)
lines: Here f(x) = secx ⇒ f′(x) = secx tanx
steps.why: secx tanx is the standard derivative of secx, so the bracket secx+secx tanx is f(x)+f′(x) for f(x)=secx.
common_mistakes: Not recognising secx tanx as the derivative of secx, and attempting integration by parts instead.
Taking f(x)=tanx by mistake, since tanx also appears in the bracket.
steps.memory_tip: secx tanx is ONE standard derivative (of secx) — memorise it as a single unit, not as two separate factors.

steps.label: Apply the formula for the final answer

lines.text: ∴ ∫ eˣ(secx+secx tanx) dx = eˣ secx + c

steps.why: Substituting f(x)=secx into ∫eˣ[f+f′]dx = eˣf(x)+c gives the final answer directly.
common_mistakes: Writing eˣ tanx instead of eˣ secx in the final line.
steps.memory_tip: The bracket has TWO terms; the answer keeps only ONE — the f(x) you identified, here secx.
